A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 26-page versions of ProDAG. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, checklist and Appendices A–I support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v6 reports original synthetic DAG experiments, Sachs flow-cytometry results, and appendix evaluations covering robustness, MUNIN data, MCMC comparisons and computation times.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results in Section 7 and Appendix G, together with the computation-time analysis in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The projected distributions, two-stage projection, ELBO, nonlinear construction and Algorithms 1–3 are retained. Section 4.2 corrects a derivative expression for the existing objective, without establishing a change to the underlying method or implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear and nonlinear synthetic DAG tasks, graph and noise variants, Sachs flow-cytometry data, and MUNIN semi-synthetic data.

E2.justification: DAGMA, DiBS, DiBS+, BayesDAG and BOSS retain the same participation and exclusions in the corresponding experiments. The Gadget comparison in Appendix G.3 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendices E–F retain the same graph sizes, sample sizes, validation scheme, model architectures, optimization settings and four evaluation metrics. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix G.1 retains the same graph-density, scale-free, non-Gaussian noise and heteroscedasticity analyses in Figures 7–15. The computational scaling analysis is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and standard errors over ten independently generated datasets for simulations and timings, and ten data splits for Sachs. Run-count disclosures and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–15 and Tables 1–4 retain the same results and uncertainty values, including the Sachs, MUNIN, Gadget and timing comparisons. No result entries or reported findings are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the acyclicity gradient from 2(I − W ◦ W)^(-1) ◦ W to 2(I − W ◦ W)^(-T) ◦ W. The inverse transpose fixes the log-determinant derivative. The theorem, propositions and appendix derivations otherwise retain the same mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about valid projected DAG distributions, scalable variational inference, uncertainty quantification and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the experimental results and qualifications concerning identifiability, likelihood misspecification, computational cost, variational approximation and nonconvex optimization remain unchanged, including Section 8 and Appendices H–I.

D1.justification: Appendices B and E retain the same implementation settings, hyperparameters, software versions, hardware and access information. Code and data links are unchanged; only the document’s own arXiv version link advances.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic spacing adjustments do not add or remove references or revise relationships to prior methods.

P1.justification: There are isolated copyedits, including an added comma in Section 3.1 and removal of 'the' before 'projection (2)' in Appendix A. Section order and the substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Mathematical typesetting and page flow change modestly. Figure 2 moves from page 6 to page 7, and Related Work begins on page 3 instead of page 2. All fifteen figures and four tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the inverse to an inverse transpose in Section 4.2 removes a mathematically incorrect gradient expression that could mislead implementation. This is a limited accuracy improvement; the empirical evidence, theoretical guarantees and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
